subject: the inside of a crowded apothecary cabinet seen head on and close, shelf above shelf filling the frame edge to edge with ranked glass specimen jars and squat stoppered bottles, every jar stoppered and sealed and every specimen suspended inside the liquid behind its glass, nothing standing loose on the shelf boards, the skulls and the bones and the loose teeth each sealed inside a jar of their own exactly like the soft specimens, no skull and no bone resting on a shelf board or standing in front of the glass, every jar's mouth and base drawn complete and unbroken so that each specimen sits wholly behind the near wall of its jar, almost every jar carrying a paper label, foxed and water stained and peeling at one corner, each label pasted flat on the outside of the glass and left unobscured with nothing inside the jar crossing in front of it, each label hand brushed with two or three characters in faded black ink in a single vertical column, the names of dried herbs and medicines, their glass clouded and ringed with old residue, and sealed inside those jars the things the cabinet keeps, one two-headed lamb foetus curled inside the tallest jar, coiled pale snakes, a jar of loose human teeth, finger bones laid out in rows, a small cracked skull with a hole bored in its crown, brass calipers and bundles of dried herbs and bone-handled instruments hung on the uprights between the shelves, cobweb and dust thick in every corner and on the near edge of the lowest shelf, every jar lit from behind by a hot saturated magenta light, deep pink and violet shading to crimson, so the liquid glows and the specimens and the shelf boards read as silhouette, deep shadow between and behind the jars
